title: Implement the xdg-terminal-exec contract so TD can be quattro's default terminal
role: No-latitude control (falsifier F1). The substantive answers are dictated by the published xdg-terminal-exec / X-TerminalArg* desktop-entry contract and by the issue's own reproduce and done-when blocks. Two deliberately open implementation questions (q7, q8) are included so an honest arm has somewhere legitimate to differ while flagging overall latitude as immaterial.
arm_visibility_note: Arms see each question's text only. Kind markings and keys never enter any arm's prompt.

q1.text: What command-line flag does Terminal Delight accept to run a command in the first pane, and what runs when it is given?

key.dictated_by: the issue's reproduce block runs `terminal-delight -e htop` and the done-when runs `xdg-terminal-exec ... -e htop`; foot's shipped entry declares X-TerminalArgExec=-e

q2.text: How is the requested application id applied to the window?

key.dictated_by: the consuming contract passes --app-id=; gpui exposes Window::set_app_id (named in the issue as the available primitive)

q3.text: How does the caller set the first pane's working directory, and how is it applied?

key.dictated_by: X-TerminalArgDir names the flag (foot declares --working-directory=); term::spawn_in(cwd) exists per the issue

q4.text: What flag sets the window title, and where is it declared for consumers?

key.dictated_by: X-TerminalArgTitle in the shipped omarchy terminal entries (foot: --title=)

q5.text: What must the installed desktop entry carry for xdg-terminal-exec to drive Terminal Delight?

key.dictated_by: the X-TerminalArg* key set carried by omarchy's shipped terminal entries, named in the issue

q6.text: What happens on a bare launch with no arguments?

key.dictated_by: the feature adds a CLI surface; the issue's proof section treats today's GUI launch as the behaviour to keep
correct_patterns: (?i)(unchanged|as today|exactly as (it does|now)|default shell|normal GUI|current behaviou?r)

q7.text: Where does argument parsing live and what parses it (hand-rolled, or a named crate)?

q8.text: How does a `-e` launch interact with saved-session adoption — does a commanded window still adopt or restore a saved session?

out_of_scope: The omarchy default-terminal setter whitelist (a separate upstream PR, tracked separately per the issue)
Any other CLI surface beyond what the xdg-terminal-exec contract needs
